newsitem.title: UK: British scientists identify kidney cancer genes.
newsitem.headline: British scientists identify kidney cancer genes.

text.p: British scientists said on Monday they had found two genes involved in the development of kidney cancer and said they would help in early diagnosis of one of the most deadly forms of the condition.
The two genes, dubbed PRCC and TFE3, could also be targeted for gene therapy, the Institute for Cancer Research said in a statement.

"Understanding the genetic changes that take place early on could help us to diagnose the disease more quickly and accurately," Colin Cooper, head of the team that discovered the genes, said in a statement.
"Because the kidney is an organ that can be removed relatively easily, catching the disease earlier means the patient has a better chance of it being treated successfully."
If kidney cancer is diagnosed and treated early, patients have a 95 percent chance of survival. But 80 to 90 percent of the patients will die within two years if it is not treated quickly.
The research, supported by the Cancer Research Campaign, was published in the September issue of the journal Human Molecular Genetics.
Another gene, known as VHL, has also been linked with kidney cancer.
